headline: Hackers exploited PHP vulnerabilities days before patches were publicly released
summary: AWS detected exploitation attempts of the critical PHP2Shell flaws on October 17, four days before public disclosure and patch release, indicating some attackers knew about the vulnerabilities early.
details: The internet's urgent scramble to patch two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used web scripting language, was already too late to stop every attack, new details reveal.

Fixes for the two critical flaws, collectively known as PHP2Shell, were released on Wednesday. This prompted administrators and security staff to race to identify and patch vulnerable websites and apps.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) research, published Wednesday evening, indicates that at least one actor had started attempting to exploit these bugs on October 17. This was four days before the public release of patches.

AWS analysts spotted the October 17 exploitation on one of their honeypots, intentionally vulnerable web servers used to study attack methods. The attempt originated from an IP address linked to a commercial anonymization network.

It remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure, but the activity suggests a threat actor was involved. Proof-of-concept exploits for PHP2Shell began emerging publicly hours before the official disclosure.
AWS honeypots were hit with multiple exploitation attempts from various anonymized providers, likely indicating different actors. AWS noted that PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.

AWS emphasizes that coordinated vulnerability disclosure must evolve and speed up. This is due to global access to AI tools that can accelerate vulnerability analysis, allowing less technically proficient actors to quickly develop new exploits.

headline_marked: [[Apple & DOJ hit impasse]] over document cutoff in antitrust lawsuit
headline: Apple & DOJ hit impasse over document cutoff in antitrust lawsuit
summary: Apple and the Department of Justice have informed the court they cannot agree on the scope of discovery documents in their ongoing antitrust lawsuit, specifically regarding how recent the documents must be.
details: Apple and the Department of Justice have filed a joint notice of impasse with the court. The two parties cannot agree on the scope of document discovery in their ongoing antitrust lawsuit.

The disagreement specifically concerns how recent Apple's internal documents must be to fall within the scope of the discovery process. This procedural hurdle could impact the evidence presented in the case.
This impasse highlights the contentious nature of the legal proceedings. Both sides are seeking to define the boundaries of information exchange as the lawsuit progresses.
